Subject: Vendor onboarding: pilot access and PO question

Hi Mateo,

Thanks for the demo last week — BlueHelix is excited to pilot Redwood for semantic search across our internal docs. We have a small 3-month pilot planned (30-75k tokens/day estimated) and want to move quickly. Two quick procurement questions before we complete onboarding:

1) Does Redwood require an issued purchase order to start a paid pilot, or can we onboard on an invoice/credit-net30 arrangement for an initial month?
2) What information do you need from us for vendor setup (W9, banking, insurance, DPA, etc.)?

Our procurement team is usually strict about POs but their cadence is slow (can take 3–4 weeks). If there is a standard exception path for short pilots, that would help us start earlier.

Attaching a short SOW outline and our standard vendor onboarding form — let me know if anything is missing.

Thanks —
Elena Morales
Head of GTM Operations
BlueHelix AI
elena@bluehelix.ai
+1 (415) 555-0192

From: mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai
To: Elena Morales <elena@bluehelix.ai>
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 30 Jun 2025 10:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Vendor onboarding: pilot access and PO question

Elena — great to hear and glad the demo resonated. Quick answers: we generally require a PO for any invoice-based purchase when the contract value exceeds our PO threshold, but we do have a temporary exception path for short pilots under certain conditions.

What we typically need to onboard a vendor: completed vendor onboarding form, W-9 (or equivalent), the SOW or statement of work for the pilot, and a signed DPA if data will be ingested. If you can share the completed onboarding form and confirm the estimated spend for month 1, procurement can evaluate an exception.

If BlueHelix prefers not to wait for a PO, one common option is:
- Provide a signed SOW + prepayment for month 1 (we can invoice immediately), OR
- Sign a short-term purchase agreement and our procurement team can approve a 30-day PO submission window.

Cc'ing Priyom (procurement) to start the exception evaluation and Aditya from Sales for the SOW/contract logistics. I can also provision test keys on our hosted API for you while procurement works through paperwork.

Thanks,
Mateo Alvarez
Strategic Accounts — Enterprise
Redwood Inference
mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai

Thanks Mateo — attaching the completed onboarding form and the SOW with more detail on scope and expected monthly volume. We estimate ~$9k for month 1 and ~15–18k/month thereafter for the pilot configuration described in the SOW.

We'd like to request a temporary no-PO arrangement for the first 30 days because our PO process is tied to a budgeting window that won't clear in time. If possible, we can either: (A) prepay month 1 on receipt of invoice, or (B) accept a limited exception with the PO to follow within 30 days.

Please find attachments: vendor_onboarding_form.pdf, BlueHelix-SOW-draft.docx. Happy to jump on a short call if helpful.

Subject: RE: Vendor onboarding: pilot access and PO question

Mateo / team — I've reviewed the submitted forms and the SOW. Procurement is willing to provision a short-term exception with the following conditions:

1) Exception limit: up to $20,000 total commit for the pilot without a formal PO.
2) Financial control: BlueHelix must either prepay month 1 or provide a signed SOW and authorize invoice-net30 with a written promise to provide the PO within 30 calendar days of the first invoice date.
3) Legal / DPA: Legal needs to sign the DPA before any customer data is ingested. No production data until DPA is countersigned.
4) Risk review: Insurance and W9 must be received (we have the onboarding form but need the W9).

I've attached the procurement exception request form I will route to Finance and Legal for sign-off. If Finance approves, Procurement will issue a formal exception number and route billing instructions. If Legal requests changes to the DPA, exception approval will be contingent on final DPA execution.

Action items:
- BlueHelix: return W9 + choose prepay vs invoice-net30 (they indicated prepay is possible).
- Mateo / Sales: confirm whether Redwood can provision non-production API keys for initial testing once onboarding form is accepted.
- Marissa (Finance): please advise whether prepayment for month 1 requires an internal receivable hold or can be treated as standard revenue.

Priyom Das
Sr. Procurement Manager
Redwood Inference
procurement@redwood.ai

Attachments: procurement_exception_request.pdf

Elena — good news: procurement has provisionally approved the exception path with the conditions Priyom listed. Next steps to get you started as soon as today:

1) BlueHelix to send W9 and confirm prepayment for month 1 (we can send an invoice immediately).
2) Sign and return the DPA (I'll follow up with a DocuSign link: https://redwood.app/ds/DocuSign:BX-2025-07-02). Legal has been looped and will expedite.
3) Once onboarding docs are complete, I will provision non-production API keys and a separate billing account for the pilot.

Notes and constraints: we cannot accept production customer data until the DPA is fully executed; exception approval covers only the pilot scope in the attached SOW and expires after 30 days if a PO is not provided. If you prefer, prepayment removes the PO dependency and we can start immediately upon DPA signature.

I'll hold a 15-minute kickoff at 11:30 PT today if you'd like to confirm the operational details — confirm a time and I'll send a calendar invite.

Thanks —
